title: Sam Altman throws shade at Anthropic’s cyber model, Mythos: ‘fear-based marketing’
description: This week, during a podcast appearance, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman called out his competitor's new cybersecurity model, noting that the company was using fear to make its product sound more impressive than it actually is.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Clarifai deletes 3 million photos that OkCupid provided to train facial recognition AI, report says
description: The photo deletion comes after an FTC settlement with Clarifai. The company had asked OkCupid — whose executives had invested in Clarifai — to share data in 2014, according to court documents.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: AI Dungeon maker Latitude unveils Voyage, a platform for creating AI-powered RPGs
description: Latitude's new AI-native platform, Voyage, aims to help gamers create their very own role-playing game.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Bond, a new social media platform, wants to use AI to help you kick your doomscrolling habit
description: Bond wants you to get off the couch and get back into the real world, its creator says. The new platform's AI system is designed to motivate users to do things away from the app.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: YouTube expands its AI likeness detection technology to celebrities
description: YouTube is expanding its AI likeness detection tool to celebrities, giving talent and their reps a way to find and remove deepfakes.
author: Sarah Perez

title: GRAI believes AI can make music more social, not replace artists
description: AI music startup GRAI says fans want to remix tracks, not generate songs from scratch.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Anthropic takes $5B from Amazon and pledges $100B in cloud spending in return
description: Amazon has made another circular AI deal: It's investing another $5 billion in Anthropic. Anthropic has agreed to spend $100 billion on AWS in return.
author: Julie Bort

title: Google rolls out Gemini in Chrome in 7 new countries
description: Google is rolling out Gemini in Chrome in Australia, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, and Vietnam. The company is rolling this feature out to both desktop and iOS in all of these countries except Japan.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: It’s not just one thing — it’s another thing
description: This sentence construction ("It's not just this — it's that") has become so common in AI-generated writing that it's no longer just a clue that a piece of writing may be synthetic — it's almost a guarantee.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: NSA spies are reportedly using Anthropic’s Mythos, despite Pentagon feud
description: NSA is said to be using Anthropic's restricted Mythos AI model.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: CEO and CFO suddenly depart AI nuclear power upstart Fermi
description: The startup, co-founded by former U.S. Energy Secretary Rick Perry, has faced headwinds with its AI campus in Texas.
author: Kirsten Korosec

title: OpenAI’s existential questions
description: On the latest episode of Equity, we discuss OpenAI's latest acquisitions and whether they address "two big existential problems" for the company.
author: Anthony Ha

title: The 12-month window
description: A lot of AI startups exist partly because the foundation models haven't expanded into their category yet. As many jokingly acknowledge, that won't last forever.
author: Connie Loizos

title: Palantir posts mini-manifesto denouncing inclusivity and ‘regressive’ cultures
description: Palantir's ideological bent has come under more scrutiny as it's worked with ICE and positioned itself as a defender of "the West."
author: Anthony Ha

title: TechCrunch Mobility: Uber enters its assetmaxxing era
description: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, how AI is playing a part.
author: Kirsten Korosec

title: Tesla brings its robotaxi service to Dallas and Houston
description: The company now offers robotaxi service in three cities, all of them in Texas, after launching in Austin last year and starting to offer rides without safety drivers in January 2026.
author: Anthony Ha

title: AI chip startup Cerebras files for IPO
description: In recent months, the company announced an agreement with Amazon Web Services to use Cerebras chips in Amazon data centers, as well as a deal with OpenAI reportedly worth more than $10 billion.
author: Anthony Ha

title: Anthropic’s relationship with the Trump administration seems to be thawing
description: Despite recently being designated a supply-chain risk by the Pentagon, Anthropic is still talking to high-level members of the Trump administration.
author: Anthony Ha

title: The App Store is booming again, and AI may be why
description: New data from Appfigures shows a swell of new app launches in 2026, suggesting AI tools could be fueling a mobile software boom.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Sam Altman’s project World looks to scale its human verification empire. First stop: Tinder.
description: World, which has raised eyebrows (but also a lot of interest) with its Orb-centered anonymous verification project, is looking to expand its influence via a bevy of new partnerships.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Kevin Weil and Bill Peebles exit OpenAI as company continues to shed ‘side quests’
description: Kevin Weil and Bill Peebles are leaving OpenAI as the company shuts down Sora and folds its science team, signaling a sharp pivot away from consumer moonshots toward enterprise AI.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Sources: Cursor in talks to raise $2B+ at $50B valuation as enterprise growth surges
description: Returning backers a16z and Thrive are expected to lead the round.
author: Marina Temkin

title: ‘Tokenmaxxing’ is making developers less productive than they think
description: There's a lot more code — but it's a lot more expensive and requires a lot more rewriting.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Tokenmaxxing, OpenAI’s shopping spree, and the AI Anxiety Gap
description: The gap between AI insiders and everyone else is widening, and the spending, suspicion, and even new vocabulary are starting to show it. While OpenAI is busy buying up everything from finance apps to talk shows, a certain shoe company just rebranded as an AI infrastructure play, and Anthropic unveiled a model it says is too powerful to release publicly …but apparently not too […]
author: Anthony Ha, Theresa Loconsolo, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O'Kane

title: Anthropic launches Claude Design, a new product for creating quick visuals
description: The company says Claude Design is intended to help people like founders and product managers without a design background share their ideas more easily.
author: Aisha Malik

title: Are we tokenmaxxing our way to nowhere?
description: The gap between AI insiders and everyone else is widening, and the spending, suspicion, and even new vocabulary are starting to show it. While OpenAI is busy buying up everything from finance apps to talk shows, a certain shoe company just rebranded as an AI infrastructure play, and Anthropic unveiled a model it says is too powerful to release publicly …but apparently not too […]
author: Theresa Loconsolo

title: Factory hits $1.5B valuation to build AI coding for enterprises
description: The three-year-old startup raised $150 million led by Khosla Ventures.
author: Marina Temkin

title: Luma launches AI-powered production studio with faith-focused Wonder Project
description: The studio's first project will be about Moses and star Academy Award-winner Ben Kingsley, to be released this spring on Prime Video.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Upscale AI in talks to raise at $2B valuation, says report
description: AI infrastructure company Upscale AI is reportedly in talks to raise its third funding round since launching just seven months ago.
author: Dominic-Madori Davis

title: Physical Intelligence, a hot robotics startup, says its new robot brain can figure out tasks it was never taught
description: The new model, called π0.7, represents what the company describes as an early but meaningful step toward the long-sought goal of a general-purpose robot brain.
author: Connie Loizos
